featured_reviews.review_text:
This place has become a personal favorite when it comes to seafood—I've been a regular here, and it never disappoints!

The variety they offer is fantastic, and the quality is consistently top-notch. Despite the 1+1 seating setup, the place is always crowded, which speaks volumes about how popular it is. If you're a fan of South Indian-style seafood, you're in for a treat—their preparations really stand out.

Some dishes you must try include the Seafood Soup, the rich and flavorful Seafood Gassi, and the tangy Pulli Munchi. We were also recommended the Prawns Kadipatta—it was absolutely delicious. If you’re into crab, they’ve got some great options there too!

What I love most is that it's not just tasty, but also easy on the wallet. Great seafood, great flavors, and great value—what more can you ask for?

featured_reviews.name: Siddhesh Kotian
featured_reviews.review_text:
Recently visited Harish Lunch Home for a non-veg dinner, and I have to say, my experience was quite mixed. While the restaurant does have a parking facility and offers both bar and family seating sections, the food and service left much to be desired.
This place is known for its seafood and bar setup, so I had some expectations going in. We ordered a variety of dishes:
•	Manchow Soup
•	Chicken Ghee Roast
•	Butter Garlic Prawns
•	Bombil Fry
•	Chicken Crispy
•	Egg Fried Rice

Out of everything, only the soup was passable. The chicken ghee roast was underwhelming—the masala wasn’t cooked properly. Butter garlic prawns lacked flavor and freshness, and the bombil fry didn’t meet the usual seafood standard either.

The chicken crispy was the biggest disappointment. It was hard and chewy, nowhere near the crispy texture we expected—it honestly ruined the mood of the meal.

For the main course, we ordered egg fried rice, but the waiter failed to guide us properly with portion sizes, especially considering we were a big family. This led to a shortage and overall dining discomfort.

In short, service was poor, food was mostly below average, and portion sizes were not family-friendly.
I would not recommend this place for a proper family dinner. If you’re looking for quality food and attentive service, I suggest you explore other options.

Visited China Dine at Hanuman Road and ordered the Prawns Triple Schezwan Rice.
The restaurant is simple and mainly suits quick, casual dining.
Service was okay and the staff were reasonably prompt.
Presentation of the dish was also fine, nothing fancy but acceptable.
However, the taste was quite disappointing.
The Schezwan flavor was very pale, lacking the usual spice and punch.
The prawns did not taste fresh and had very mild seasoning.
The gravy was thin and watery instead of rich and flavorful.
The rice and sauce did not blend well together.
Overall, the dish felt bland and lacked depth.
Portion size was alright, but taste did not match the price.
If someone prefers strong, spicy Schezwan-style food, this will fall short.
The dish definitely needs better seasoning and fresher prawns.
There are better places nearby for Indo-Chinese with stronger flavor.
Overall: 2/5 for taste, though service and presentation were okay.

featured_reviews.name: Omkar Naik
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited Dan Dan Chinese today on the occasion of Ram Navami, as many nearby Chinese food corners were closed. I decided to give this place a try, and I ordered two dishes: American Choupsey and Chicken Hakka Noodles.

Both dishes were delicious, and I must say, it was my first time trying Choupsey, which I highly recommend to anyone visiting this place. The Chicken Hakka Noodles were also tasty, and they offer good quality and quantity. The portion sizes are quite generous, so one person may struggle to finish a dish — it's best to come with a companion or plan to parcel the leftover food.

As a local guide on Google Maps and someone who likes to share detailed reviews, I'd like to highlight a few points that may be helpful for potential customers, and also for the owner to consider:

1. Lack of Air Conditioning: There is no air conditioning in the restaurant, and in the humid climate of Vile Parle East, it can get uncomfortable, especially near the fan area. Adding an air conditioning system could significantly improve the dining experience.

2. Cold Drinks: The restaurant doesn't offer cold drinks on the menu but provides them by bringing them from an outside source. While I appreciate that they offer this option when many others refuse, it would be more convenient if they stocked cold drinks on-site.

3. Slow Service: The food took quite a long time to be served, and there was no dedicated staff member to assist customers. There was an uncle helping out, but he was juggling multiple tasks — taking orders, answering calls, handling the kitchen, and managing bills. This made the service a bit frustrating at times, and I ended up packing my noodles to go. It would be beneficial to have an extra staff member to assist with customer service.

4. Mosquitoes: The restaurant is open, and with no gates, mosquitoes can be a problem. The plants outside, while adding to the aesthetic, also provide a hiding place for mosquitoes. Addressing this issue, perhaps with a net or better control, would improve the comfort of diners.

5. Order Assistance: Typically, restaurants guide customers on specials, combos, and menu items when taking orders. However, I was not informed about the combos or daily specials until after my order was placed. It would be helpful if the staff proactively shared this information to enhance the dining experience.

6. Customer Service: While the food was good, there were some basic service issues. No one asked if I wanted water, and there were no tissues or sauces available on the table. That said, I’d like to commend the uncle at the counter, who made an effort to clean my plate, spoon, and fork before serving. His politeness and attention to detail were appreciated.

Suggestions for Improvement:

Install air conditioning to improve comfort in the humid climate.

Stock cold drinks on-site to make it more convenient for customers.

Reduce the waiting time and consider adding more staff for customer service.

Address the mosquito issue, perhaps with better pest control or netting.

Ensure that customers are informed about specials and combos when ordering.

Provide basic amenities like water, tissues, and sauces to enhance the overall dining experience.

Overall, Dan Dan Chinese offers tasty food, but there are some areas for improvement, especially regarding service, comfort, and customer care. With a few adjustments, it could provide a much more enjoyable dining experience.

Note: I’ve added photos of the restaurant, the food I ordered, and the menu for reference to help others get a better idea before visiting.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Dropped by this gem the other day we were at Juhu beach and this one is cited at a walk of 5 mins from the Novotel end. Talking about the ambience first, they have indoor as well as outdoor dining area. The entire space looks extremely vibrant and full of colours which looks absolutely beautiful. Coming to the f&b, for our first round of drinks we ordered for Kung Fu Panda which was a gin-based cocktail having refreshing elements like Basil, lemongrass ginger, star anise and passionfruit. Loved the way it was presented which made it totally gramworthy. Next, we had Golden dynasty from their Chinese new years menu, this one was vodka base and had lovely taste as it had citrusy elements. The food menu here is wide spread and offers almost everything you could think of. We tried their Philadelphia Cream cheese and miso Dimsums and hands down these are one of the finest cheese dimsums we have tried in a while. Next we had Crab Salad and tempura prawn sushi which also had cream cheese drizzled on top of it. Mild and mellow flavour profile yet the chef managed to make it so delectable. This one was so good that we had to repeat it. Upon or servers recommendation, we tried Prawns in butter garlic which was wok tossed prawns drenched in butter garlic sauce. Simple and perfect which can't go wrong. Later for the mains, we tried Exotic Mushroom clay pot rice which was topped with truffle butter sauce. The pot rice had a generous amount of veggies and especially mushrooms. We lastly ordered for Chilli garlic noodles which were thin noodles wok tossed in chilli garlic sauce along with chicken - this was totally worth every penny. Now for round two of drinks we tried chin chin gin and Oogway’s paloma which was again gin base cocktail. Both the cocktails were a solid 10.
For dessert, we had Nutella wellcake which was soft and gooey cake drenched in Nutella. Overall it was a lovely dining experience and we will be coming here again for sure.

A Culinary Gem at Goma – A Must-Visit for Pan-Asian Enthusiasts

I recently dined at Goma, nestled within the Radisson Hotel Mumbai Goregaon, and it was an unforgettable experience.  The restaurant's interiors exude elegance, setting the perfect ambiance for a delightful meal.

Our culinary journey began with the prawns  soup—a harmonious blend of flavors that awakened the palate.  The chicken gyoza and Edamame were perfectly steamed, offering a savory bite that paired wonderfully with the accompanying sauces.

For the main course, the vegetarian sushi boat was a visual and gastronomic delight.  The assortment was generous, and each piece showcased the freshness and quality one expects from top-tier sushi.  The fish in butter garlic sauce melted in the mouth, rich and flavorful, while the lamb chops were tender and seasoned to perfection.  The Hakka noodles stood out with their impeccable texture and taste, complemented by a hearty stew-like gravy brimming with fresh vegetables—a wholesome touch that added both flavor and nutrition.

A highlight of our visit was the ongoing Mango Mania Festival.  The pull me up mango cake was a tropical dream, moist and bursting with mango goodness.  The mango panna cotta was silky smooth, offering a refreshing end to our meal.

Goma masterfully blends traditional Japanese accents with innovative fusion cuisine, making it a standout dining destination in Mumbai.  Highly recommended for those seeking a memorable Pan-Asian culinary experience.

featured_reviews.name: Ritu Gagwani
featured_reviews.review_text:
An Asian restaurant located inside Radisson, featuring excellent interiors and elegant décor. From the moment you enter, the space exudes a top-notch vibe and gives you a feeling of being a class apart. The ambience is definitely one of the highlights. The menu is well-curated and the service is generally good, adding to the overall experience.

However, coming to the food—starting with the soups—we ordered the Tom Kha, which leaned a bit too much on the sweeter side. The Veg Manchow Soup was just average and could have been much better, especially considering the ambience and pricing.

We also tried the Corn and Chestnut Dumplings, which unfortunately felt stale and quite sticky. We’ve had the same dumplings at other places where they tasted far better. We ordered a few other dishes as well, which were all just about okay and did not really stand out.

One dish we absolutely loved was the Black Garlic Dumplings, which came from the chef’s side—these were truly outstanding and easily the highlight of the meal.

For the mains, we ordered Blue Pea Rice with Mapo Tofu. The rice felt quite dry and slightly undercooked, while the Mapo Tofu definitely needs serious improvement in terms of flavour and texture.
Even a simple mocktail like a Mojito had to be changed at least four times, which was disappointing.
The chocolate dessert was another great highlight— the dark chocolate tart was absolutely lovely, and it was honestly hard to resist stopping at just one.
Overall, while the place scores high on ambience and décor, it needs significant improvement in food quality and consistency to truly justify its pricing.
